what_happened.line: The board found the dog dangerous, 4-0 with one abstention, and continued the hearing to October 15 at 7:30 for the penalty.
Testimony in the dog hearing is closed; the final penalty determination comes on October 15.
The board approved removal of the eight public trees Unitil recommended, and approved removing brush three inches or less, 4-1.
The board appointed citizen members to the TC Passios building design committee and ratified the principal clerk appointment.
The board recommended the Saliba property acquisition article, 4-0 with one abstention, and deferred its recommendation on the Butterfly Lane article.

why_it_matters: The Saliba purchase would be authorized in full and carried until state grants reimburse it, with the remainder borrowed, so it may affect future debt payments paid mostly from taxes.
The dog penalty is still undecided, and the tree and brush decisions touch roadside trees and scenic roads, with five trees the planning board did not approve still unsettled.
watch_next: October 15 at 7:30: the board's final penalty determination in the dangerous dog hearing.
The special town meeting vote on the warrant articles, including Saliba, and the board's deferred recommendation on the Butterfly Lane article.

what_happened.line: The Select Board withdrew a motion to adopt special event permit guidelines and will rework the definition for a July workshop.
Lake Shirley residents spent long public comment on a dispute with the Conservation Commission over an order of conditions and an alleged conflict of interest.
The board approved a Unitil pole location on Pine Grove Road, with one member voting no, and a one-day wine and malt license for June 8.
The board voted to invite talent bank applicants to interview in the Conservation Commission reappointment process.
The board released listed executive session minutes, then went into executive session on litigation by roll call vote.

why_it_matters: Special event rules decide what events, such as those on Holman Street, may be held and what notice abutters get, and the definition is still unsettled.
Conservation Commission seats and orders of conditions affect lakefront owners, and the reappointment interviews change how residents can apply for those seats.

A state earmark for the Eagle House senior center, to be reimbursed against expenses by June 30, will affect free cash, and higher supply rates for electricity and gas from December 1 touch the FY20 budget.
watch_next: The July workshop on the special event permit definition, with the date still to be set with the town manager.

Members agreed the reappointment process goes on the June 4 agenda, with reappointments likely June 18 under a light-touch process.
The board voted on Finance Committee appointing-committee and MPO representative seats, and agreed to put labor counsel and a possible new meeting location on future agendas.
The board heard that the town's MS4 stormwater compliance plan involves engineering consulting over five years, and that a stormwater utility fee was discussed.

why_it_matters: A stormwater utility fee, if pursued, would be a new charge on property owners, and pay-as-you-throw bag fees are also due back before the board in June.
The electrical system at the TC Passios building is past its lifespan, so an upgrade is likely to need funding, probably through the town budget, which is mostly taxes.

what_happened.line: The Select Board split 2-2 on tabling the town manager's evaluation, then 2-2 on reading it tonight and discussing it next week; both motions failed.
The chair read the full composite evaluation into the record, and the board agreed to seek a consensus next week, with edits going to the chair meanwhile.
The board approved a toll booth, a cruise night road closure and an appointment to the Agricultural Commission; two other appointment votes were not audible.
The board approved an entertainment license for a three-day family event, amended to cap amplified music at eight hours a day.
The quarterly financial report was held over to next week and is to go first on the agenda; the missing ballot questions were left to the new board.

why_it_matters: The town manager's evaluation is the board's main review of who runs town departments, and its final form will not be set until the board meets again.
Ballot questions that did not reach the Town Meeting ballot will not be addressed until after the election, so voters should not expect them on this cycle's ballot.
The quarterly financial report, which shows how the current budget is tracking, was delayed by a week.
watch_next: Next week's Select Board meeting: discussion and consensus on the composite evaluation, and the quarterly financial report first on the agenda.
